target_group: Landholding farmer families (initially <2 ha; all farmers from June 2019)
description: Rs 6000/year in three equal instalments by DBT
stated_goal: Supplement farm income and finance inputs
outcome_summary: UP survey: 30% received benefit within 3 months; 52% of 1st (peak-season) instalment spent on agriculture vs 23% of 2nd (off-season); with KVK extension modern-input adoption 'significantly higher' by 36%
outcome_metric: Share of instalment spent on agriculture
side_effects: Large share of off-season instalment went to consumption (39%) and health/education (19%)
public_reaction: High demand: 93% of non-beneficiaries had applied
source_title: Giving the multiplier effect to PM-KISAN (IFPRI blog, Varshney, Kumar, Joshi, Roy, 2020)

target_group: Farmers growing notified crops (in practice wheat and rice)
description: Government announces MSP and FCI/state agencies procure grain
stated_goal: Price assurance for farmers and food-security stocks
outcome_summary: Shanta Kumar HLC (2015): only 6% of farmers get MSP; FCI procured 12% of wheat and 2% of paddy production
side_effects: Bias to wheat/rice; 21 other notified crops neglected; PDS leakage estimated 40-50%
public_reaction: Committee's proposals to restructure FCI/PDS were contested (reaction not verified from opened source)
source_title: Reduce food security benefits from 67% to 40% population, says panel on restructuring FCI (Down To Earth, 22 Jan 2015)

policy_name: Agricultural Debt Waiver and Debt Relief Scheme (ADWDRS)
description: Cancellation of farm loans worth US$16-17 billion; banks fully recapitalised
stated_goal: Relieve farm distress and restore credit access
outcome_summary: District panel 2001-2012: household debt fell and total lending rose but no increase in investment, consumption or wages; high-bailout districts got 36 cents new lending per $1 written off vs ~$4 in low-bailout districts
outcome_metric: New lending per $1 written off (above- vs below-median bailout districts)
side_effects: Strategic default after waiver in high-bailout districts; banks rationed credit toward less risky regions
public_reaction: Not verified from opened source
source_title: Economic effects of India's farm loan bailout: business as usual? (World Bank All About Finance blog, Gine & Kanz)

policy_name: Crop insurance schemes NAIS/MNAIS/WBCIS (precursors of PM Fasal Bima Yojana)
description: Premium-subsidised yield/weather crop insurance via AIC and private insurers
stated_goal: Protect farmers against crop loss
outcome_summary: CAG audit 2011-12 to 2015-16 (9 states): coverage only 8-22% of farmers (NAIS 2-13%); delays at every stage of claims; funds released to private insurers without verifying claims
side_effects: AIC retained Rs 2519 crore (18% of premium) under NAIS 1999-2016; private insurers received large funds without audit
public_reaction: Not verified from opened source
source_title: PRS summary of CAG Report on Agriculture Crop Insurance Schemes (Report No. 7 of 2017)

description: Mandatory neem coating of subsidised urea
stated_goal: Curb diversion of subsidised urea and improve nitrogen use efficiency
outcome_summary: Bihar, kharif 2015 vs 2014 (400 households, no control): urea use per acre fell 6.74% (paddy) and 10.51% (maize); yields rose 3.33% (paddy) and 5.30% (maize); net returns +6.37%
outcome_metric: Change in urea use per acre
side_effects: NCU sold 16-22% above normal urea (vs stipulated 5-6%); diversion curbed but not confirmed eliminated
public_reaction: 74.75% rated quality good; 42% said price high
source_title: Impact of Neem-Coated Urea on Production, Productivity and Soil Health in Bihar (AERC Bhagalpur, Study No. 41, Jan 2017)

description: Soil testing and crop-wise fertiliser recommendations on a card
stated_goal: Balanced fertiliser use and higher soil productivity
outcome_summary: Experimental evaluation in Bihar found no evidence of any impact of SHC on fertiliser use
outcome_value: No significant effect (no numbers on page)
side_effects: Recommendations not understood or trusted; credit constraints limit action
public_reaction: Not verified from opened source
source_title: Can information help reduce imbalanced application of fertilisers in India: Experimental evidence from Bihar (IGC, Fishman et al., 2019)

description: Allowed trade outside APMC markets, contract farming framework, limited stock limits under Essential Commodities Act
stated_goal: Liberalise agricultural marketing and attract private investment
outcome_summary: Laws never implemented: Supreme Court stayed them Jan 2021; repealed by Parliament 29 Nov 2021
side_effects: Repeal passed without parliamentary discussion
public_reaction: Year-long protest at Delhi borders; repealed after mass mobilisation
game_theory_lens: bargaining / war of attrition with collective action
source_title: The Farm Laws Repeal Bill, 2021 (PRS Legislative Research)

description: Repeal of the three 2020 farm Acts after protests
stated_goal: Restore status quo marketing regime
outcome_summary: Government withdrew reforms after year-long, longest-running protest; PM said government 'not able to convince farmers'
side_effects: Policy reversal; reform credibility lost
public_reaction: Mass protest; farmers feared corporate exploitation; opposition criticised repeal without debate
game_theory_lens: bargaining / war of attrition with collective action
source_title: India's parliament passes bill officially repealing controversial farm laws after year of protests (Yahoo News, 29 Nov 2021)

target_group: Farmers, traders and commission agents at APMC mandis
description: Online trading platform integrating APMC mandis
stated_goal: Better price discovery and a unified national market
outcome_summary: Survey of 856 farmers in 6 states: participants got ~5.5% higher prices than pre-adoption; secondary mandi data showed price falls and no clear trend after e-NAM; 44% rated it better than manual mandis
side_effects: Payment delays, cumbersome online payment, poor assaying and connectivity; only 22% received quality report
public_reaction: Satisfaction 16% in UP and nil in MP; high in other surveyed states
source_title: Electronic National Agricultural Market (e-NAM): A Review of Performance and Prospects (IEG/AERC Delhi for MoA&FW, June 2020)

description: Rs 4000 per acre per season paid by cheque based on land records
stated_goal: Fund pre-season input costs
outcome_summary: RCT of phone-call monitoring of officials (~50,000 calls, May-June 2018): receipt 84.3% monitored vs 83% unmonitored; ~17,000 more farmers paid and US$3.9m more before monsoon at 3.6 cents per extra dollar
side_effects: Not reported
public_reaction: Not verified from opened source
source_title: Testing the impact of phone calls on service delivery in India (World Bank Let's Talk Development blog)

policy_name: Rythu Bandhu investment support (coverage and tenancy)
description: Rs 4000 per acre per season paid on the basis of land records
stated_goal: Fund pre-season input costs and reduce informal debt
outcome_summary: Village study: 72.28% of surveyed land covered (85.53% for large holdings); >51.5% of tribal land excluded; informal borrowing among small farmers fell 84.7% to 70.2% (2015-2020) but barely for marginal (91.8% to 90.8%)
side_effects: Tenants (~24% of farm households) excluded; benefits skewed to larger landowners
public_reaction: Not verified from opened source
game_theory_lens: bargaining / incidence between landlord and tenant
source_title: Evaluation of Rythu Bandhu Scheme (CESS Policy Brief No. 18, Sreenivasulu, May 2026)

policy_name: KALIA (Krushak Assistance for Livelihood and Income Augmentation)
target_group: Small/marginal cultivators, landless households, vulnerable households
description: Rs 5000 per family per season (cultivators); Rs 12500 over 3 years (landless); Rs 10000 (vulnerable)
stated_goal: Augment farm income and livelihoods
outcome_summary: CAG: Rs 9333.01 crore disbursed to 65.64 lakh beneficiaries 2018-22; Rs 782.26 crore paid to 12.72 lakh ineligible beneficiaries; income objective could not be assessed
side_effects: Income-tax payers, officials and multiple household members paid; 37053 eligible not paid; only 3.96 of 18 lakh landless trained; recovery 'remote'
public_reaction: Opposition alleged hasty, election-driven implementation (The Wire 2019)
source_title: CAG Compliance Audit Report, Govt of Odisha, year ended March 2022, Chapter II (KALIA)

policy_name: Mera Pani Meri Virasat (crop diversification incentive)
description: Rs 8000 per acre for shifting paddy area to cotton, maize, pulses, oilseeds, vegetables, fodder or agro-forestry
stated_goal: Conserve groundwater by reducing paddy area
outcome_summary: Season reported Dec 2025: 19,670 acres (13,500 farmers) verified against a 1 lakh-acre target (<20%); no district reached 50% of target
side_effects: ~38% of claims found false on physical verification
public_reaction: Lukewarm; farmers stayed with paddy due to assured MSP procurement and cotton losses
game_theory_lens: participation constraint vs outside option (MSP paddy)
source_title: Few takers for Haryana's crop diversification plan, only 20% of target achieved (The Tribune, 11 Dec 2025)

policy_name: Punjab Preservation of Subsoil Water Act (paddy transplanting date ban)
target_group: Paddy growers in Punjab (similar Haryana law)
description: Bans paddy transplanting before mid-June
stated_goal: Preserve groundwater
outcome_summary: Border-area comparison with neighbouring states: ban caused both delay and an increase in crop residue burning in winter months (effect sizes not on page opened)
outcome_metric: Crop residue burning timing and incidence
side_effects: Shorter window between harvest and wheat sowing pushed stubble burning into winter, worsening air pollution
public_reaction: Not verified from opened source
source_title: Unintended Consequences of Indian Groundwater Preservation Law on Crop Residue Burning (Agarwala, Bhattacharjee, Dasgupta, Ashoka Univ. WP 61, 2021)

description: Free LPG connections to poor women with loan for stove/first refill recovered from refill subsidy
stated_goal: Shift poor households from solid fuels to clean LPG cooking
outcome_summary: CAG audit (May 2016-Dec 2018): 3.78 crore connections issued; LPG coverage rose from 62% (May 2016) to 94% (Mar 2019); but average refills by PMUY households fell from 3.9 (2016-17) to 3.4 (2017-18) to 3.0 (2018-19) vs 6.7-7.5 for non-PMUY
outcome_metric: Average annual LPG refills per PMUY household
side_effects: Low sustained use; ~14 lakh beneficiaries consumed 3-41 cylinders/month and ~2 lakh >12/yr (diversion risk to commercial use); Rs 1,235 crore loan-recovery shortfall; 47% connections took >30 days to install
public_reaction: Government cited large beneficiary numbers as success (per Down To Earth); CAG urged shift from connections to sustained use
game_theory_lens: Adoption vs. sustained use under price constraint (subsidy leakage/diversion)
source_title: PRS India summary of CAG Performance Audit on PMUY (Report submitted 11 Dec 2019)

description: Free LPG connections; refill purchases at market price minus subsidy
stated_goal: Sustained clean cooking fuel use
outcome_summary: Among 3.18 crore beneficiaries with >=1 year of connection by 31 Dec 2018, 17.61% (~56 lakh) never took a second refill and 33.02% (~1.05 crore) took only 1-3 refills; average 3.21 refills/yr
side_effects: Seven of 11 states below-average consumption (Chhattisgarh, MP, Jharkhand, Odisha, Assam, WB, Maharashtra)
public_reaction: NDA govt claimed success citing beneficiary counts; no direct govt response reported
game_theory_lens: Adoption vs. sustained use under price constraint (subsidy leakage/diversion)
source_title: Down To Earth: LPG connections not only success metric: CAG on Ujjwala

policy_name: UJALA (Unnat Jyoti by Affordable LEDs for All)
description: Bulk procurement by EESL and sale of LED bulbs at low price to households
stated_goal: Reduce household electricity use and peak demand via efficient lighting
outcome_summary: As of PIB release (Jan 2022): 36.78 crore LEDs distributed; 47,778 million kWh/yr saved; 9,565 MW peak demand avoided; ~3.86 crore t CO2/yr reduced; LED retail price fell from Rs 300-350 to Rs 70-80; procurement price fell ~90% (Rs 310 to Rs 38, 2014-2017)
side_effects: Savings are engineering estimates (deemed savings), not metered; rebound effects not measured in source
public_reaction: Not documented in sources opened
source_title: PIB, Ministry of Power: UJALA completes 7 years

description: Separate electricity feeders for farm pumps vs. rural homes/non-farm users; rationed but high-quality three-phase power to farms, continuous power to homes
stated_goal: Improve rural power supply quality while rationing farm power to curb subsidy and groundwater overdraft
outcome_summary: Difference-in-differences on IHDS 2004-05 and 2011-12: no increase in electric pump ownership; diesel pump ownership fell; tubewell ownership and tubewell irrigation rose; per-acre cost of purchased irrigation water rose; net farm income per acre fell on average (more for medium-large farmers); yields not lower
outcome_value: Decreased on average (effect size not given on page)
side_effects: Higher water purchase costs for farmers; water markets shifted
public_reaction: Not documented in sources opened
source_title: World Bank seminar: Impact of farm electricity supply management on farm households (Chindarkar & Chen)

description: USD 260 million invested to separate agricultural and non-agricultural feeders
stated_goal: 24/7 three-phase power for rural households; rationed farm power
outcome_summary: IWMI reports the scheme reduced farm power subsidy and capped groundwater overdraft (no quantities given); Gujarat agricultural growth ~10% p.a. 2000/01-2006/07 vs 2.9% nationally (correlational, not attributed causally)
side_effects: Not quantified in source
public_reaction: Not documented in sources opened
source_title: IWMI Success Stories Issue 9 (2011): Innovative electricity scheme sparks rural development

target_group: Farmers with agricultural tubewells on free power
description: Voluntary metering with power quota per HP; farmers paid Rs 4 per unit saved below quota while power stays free
stated_goal: Reduce groundwater and electricity use without removing free power
outcome_summary: Pilot kharif 2018: 173 farmers on 6 feeders (Jalandhar, Hoshiarpur, Fatehgarh Sahib) saved ~1.75 lakh units and received ~Rs 7 lakh; 40 more enrolled for rabi. J-PAL RCT across 300 feeders listed as ongoing with results forthcoming
side_effects: Selection: voluntary enrolment likely attracts farmers already below quota (inference); small uptake
public_reaction: Positive farmer testimonials reported; low enrollment
game_theory_lens: Pigouvian pricing via opt-in payment for conservation (commons/CPR)
source_title: J-PAL South Asia / Indian Express (4 Jan 2019) on PBPK pilot

description: Cars allowed on alternate days by odd/even licence plate, daytime hours, two-week trials
stated_goal: Reduce vehicular air pollution
outcome_summary: January 2016 trial: fine particle (PM2.5) concentrations 14-16% lower during enforced hours relative to non-enforced night hours and satellite cities; no effect at night
side_effects: Effect limited to winter; temporary only
public_reaction: Not documented in sources opened
game_theory_lens: Negative externality (traffic pollution) under quantity rationing
source_title: EPIC India: Did odd-even clean Delhi's air? Analysis evaluates

description: Second two-week trial in April 2016
stated_goal: Reduce vehicular air pollution
outcome_summary: April 2016 trial: no detectable effect on air quality; authors attribute to faster summer dispersion
side_effects: Suggests value only as winter emergency measure
public_reaction: Not documented in sources opened
game_theory_lens: Negative externality (traffic pollution) under quantity rationing
source_title: EPIC India: Did odd-even clean Delhi's air? Analysis evaluates

description: Plant-specific energy-intensity targets; over-achievers earn tradable Energy Saving Certificates (ESCerts), under-achievers buy them or pay penalty
stated_goal: Reduce industrial energy intensity
outcome_summary: Cycle I (to Mar 2015): 478 units in 8 sectors saved 8.67 Mtoe vs 6.686 Mtoe target (+30%), ~31 Mt CO2 avoided, ~13 lakh ESCerts traded (~Rs 100 crore). Cycle II: 621 DCs saved ~13.28 Mtoe vs 8.869 Mtoe target, ~61.34 Mt CO2 avoided
outcome_value: Cycle I 8.67 vs 6.686 Mtoe; Cycle II 13.28 vs 8.869 Mtoe
side_effects: Lenient targets (see CSE row); over-achievement may reflect soft baselines
public_reaction: Not documented in sources opened
source_title: BEE: Brief Note on PAT Scheme

description: PAT targets for thermal power plants
stated_goal: Improve heat rate of thermal power plants
outcome_summary: CSE (2021): TPPs saved 3.06 Mtoe vs 3.211 Mtoe target in Cycle I (~5% short) and 3.519 vs 3.13 Mtoe in Cycle II; CO2 cut only ~1.4-1.6% of power-sector emissions; 21 (C-I) and 46 (C-II) plants complied by buying ESCerts; ~80% of TPP targets laxer than CEA benchmarks; no TPP penalised
side_effects: Cheap ESCerts (~Rs 700 avg vs ~Rs 4,020/toe abatement cost at one plant) made buying cheaper than saving; Cycle II ESCert surplus 5.84 lakh
public_reaction: CSE critical of lax targets and weak penalties
game_theory_lens: Cap-and-trade with lax cap (regulatory capture / weak enforcement)
source_title: CSE (2021): PAT Scheme in Thermal Power Plants: A Critical Analysis

description: City clean-air action plans with performance-linked funding (NCAP + XV Finance Commission grants)
stated_goal: 20-30% PM10 reduction by 2024-25 vs 2017-18, revised to up to 40% or NAAQS by 2025-26
outcome_summary: CREA (Jan 2026), 100 cities with adequate data: 77 saw PM10 decline (68 still above NAAQS), 23 saw increase; 51 met 20-30% target, 23 met revised 40% target, 12 met PM10 NAAQS. Rs 19,614 crore earmarked, Rs 13,415 crore released, Rs 9,929 crore (74%) utilised
side_effects: 68% of spend on road dust management (PM10 focus over combustion sources); 28 cities lack continuous monitors
public_reaction: Not documented in sources opened
game_theory_lens: Transboundary public good (airshed free-riding across jurisdictions)
source_title: CREA: Tracing the Hazy Air 2026 - Progress Report on NCAP

description: Central financial assistance for standalone solar pumps, solarising grid pumps, and farmer-owned decentralised solar plants
stated_goal: 10,000 MW decentralised solar (Comp A); 1.5 lakh grid pumps solarised (Comp C)
outcome_summary: Estimates Committee (Dec 2025): Component A achieved 641 MW vs 10,000 MW target (July 2025); Component C only 60,828 pumps sanctioned vs 1.5 lakh target
outcome_metric: Component A capacity achieved vs target
side_effects: No CFA for Comp A and land conversion costs deter farmers; under Comp C farmers bear ~70% cost where states add nothing; high evacuation costs
public_reaction: Parliamentary committee critical of slow progress
source_title: PRS India summary of Estimates Committee report on PM-KUSUM and PM Surya Ghar (4 Dec 2025)

description: Decentralised water-harvesting works (deepening, check dams, desilting) in villages
stated_goal: Make Maharashtra drought-free by 2019
outcome_summary: CAG found the scheme had little impact on raising groundwater levels or making villages drought-free despite Rs 9,633.75 crore spent; also flagged lack of transparency
outcome_value: Little impact despite Rs 9,633.75 crore spend (village-level numbers not verified)
side_effects: CAG flagged lack of transparency (per The Wire headline)
public_reaction: Fadnavis said it would have succeeded had it not been stopped midway; opposition corruption allegations and a probe appear in news headlines (not opened)
source_title: India Water Portal: Jalyukt Shivar Abhiyan a low impact, high expenditure scheme: CAG

description: Functional household tap connections (FHTC) to every rural household, centre-state funded
stated_goal: Har Ghar Jal: tap water to all rural households
outcome_summary: CAG Maharashtra audit: claimed 85.15% FHTC by Mar 2024 but ~69% after excluding 27.74 lakh private/own-source connections; no baseline surveys in test-checked districts; 13 schemes sanctioned without secured sources; no O&M policy
side_effects: Inflated coverage via counting private connections; non-potable supply where no treatment plants
public_reaction: Not documented in sources opened
source_title: PSU Watch: CAG report on Maharashtra's Jal Jeevan Mission flags planning failures, inflated coverage claims

target_group: EV buyers and manufacturers; public transport agencies
description: Demand incentives on EV purchase contingent on phased manufacturing localisation; capital support for e-buses and charging
stated_goal: Accelerate EV adoption and domestic EV manufacturing
outcome_summary: CAG Report No. 10 of 2026: Rs 467.96 crore paid to 5 OEMs violating localisation norms; 5,195 e-buses deployed vs revised target 6,862 (by 31 Dec 2025); only 148 of 2,877 approved charging stations commissioned; none of 8,412 OMC stations commissioned by Mar 2024
side_effects: Subsidy capture by non-compliant OEMs (Rs 190.90 crore returned by two); IEC funds underused (Rs 7.52 of 48 crore)
public_reaction: Not documented in sources opened beyond CAG noting Rs 190.90 crore returned by two OEMs
game_theory_lens: Principal-agent / moral hazard in subsidy claims
source_title: Down To Earth: CAG flags Rs 468 crore in FAME incentives to EV makers violating localisation norms

target_group: cash holders; informal economy; holders of unaccounted cash
description: On 8 Nov 2016 Rs 500 and Rs 1000 notes (86% of cash in circulation) ceased to be legal tender overnight; new notes introduced gradually.
stated_goal: Curb black money and counterfeit currency; push digital payments
outcome_summary: Districts more exposed to the cash shock saw relative falls in activity; aggregated effect was about a 2 percentage point contraction in employment and nightlights output and about 2 pp lower bank credit growth in 2016Q4 vs counterfactual; effects dissipated within months; more affected districts adopted cards/e-wallets faster.
outcome_metric: employment and nightlights output in 2016Q4 vs counterfactual
outcome_value: -2 percentage points (lower bound); bank credit -2 pp
side_effects: Short-run output and job loss; faster adoption of digital payments
public_reaction: CVoter-Huffpost-BW poll (26-27 Dec 2016, n=1281): just under 80% said it was worth the pain (lowest yet); ~3 in 4 reported little or no problem; 15% (20% of poor) still spent almost the whole day in ATM queues
game_theory_lens: signalling/credibility under a surprise policy shock
source_title: Cash and the Economy: Evidence from India's Demonetization (NBER w25370)

policy_name: Demonetisation of Rs 500/1000 notes (return of notes)
description: RBI accounting of specified bank notes (SBNs) returned to the banking system after demonetisation.
stated_goal: Extinguish unaccounted cash that would not be deposited
outcome_summary: Rs 15.31 lakh crore of Rs 15.41 lakh crore SBNs (99.3%) came back; only Rs 10,720 crore not returned, undercutting the expectation that black money would be extinguished. Note printing cost Rs 7,965 crore in 2016-17 vs Rs 3,421 crore the year before.
outcome_metric: share of demonetised notes returned to banks
side_effects: Higher printing cost; counterfeit detections in new Rs 500/2000 notes rose in 2017-18 (9,892 and 17,929 vs 199 and 638)
public_reaction: See poll in row above
source_title: 99.3% of junked Rs 500, Rs 1,000 notes returned to banks: RBI (PTI/Business Standard, citing RBI Annual Report 2017-18)

description: Destination-based multi-rate indirect tax replacing central and state indirect taxes from July 2017, governed by the GST Council.
stated_goal: Unify the national market; widen the tax base; improve compliance and revenue
outcome_summary: NIPFP WP 392 (2012-13 to 2022-23): post-GST tax buoyancy improved for Union, state and general government, but GST-to-GDP ratio not yet above the pre-GST share of comparable revenues; average C-efficiency 0.54; effective tax rate rose from 10.91% (2020-21) to 12.21% (2021-22) and 12.56% (to Q3 2022-23); policy gap larger than compliance gap.
outcome_value: C-efficiency 0.54; GST/GDP not improved over pre-GST
side_effects: Policy (rate/exemption) gap dominates revenue shortfall (per NIPFP); other side effects not verified here
public_reaction: Not verified from an opened source in this pass
game_theory_lens: coordination game (Centre-states pooling sovereignty in GST Council)
source_title: Revenue Performance Assessment of Indian GST (NIPFP WP 392, 2023)

description: Time-bound creditor-in-control corporate insolvency resolution process (CIRP) adjudicated by NCLT, administered by IBBI.
stated_goal: Faster resolution and higher recovery of stressed assets; credit discipline
outcome_summary: By 30 Sep 2025: 8,659 CIRPs admitted; 1,300 resolution plans; 2,896 liquidation orders; realisation Rs 3.99 trillion vs admitted claims Rs 12.31 trillion (~32-33%, haircut ~67%); average 603 days to resolution and 518 days to liquidation order.
outcome_metric: realisation as % of admitted claims (resolution plans)
side_effects: 43% of closures end in liquidation; long delays; old BIFR/defunct cases realise only 18.74%
public_reaction: Not verified from an opened source in this pass
game_theory_lens: bargaining game among creditors (committee of creditors) with credible exit threat
source_title: Haircuts touch 67% under IBC as creditor recovery stays low till Sep 2025 (Business Standard, citing IBBI data)

description: Cut in corporate income tax rate for domestic firms (new concessional regimes) announced Sept 2019.
stated_goal: Boost private investment and competitiveness
outcome_summary: Firm-level difference-in-differences on manufacturing firms finds the cut led to a significant increase in domestic firms' investment, larger for big firms (magnitude not reported in abstract).
outcome_value: significant increase (size not stated in abstract)
side_effects: Benefits concentrated in large firms
public_reaction: Not verified from an opened source in this pass
source_title: Effect of Tax Cut on Investment: Evidence from Indian Manufacturing Firms (NIPFP WP 390, 2023)

policy_name: Corporate income tax cut (Sept 2019) - fiscal cost
description: Ex-post estimate of revenue foregone from the 2019 cut.
stated_goal: Boost private investment
outcome_summary: The Hindu analysis (reported by The Wire): ~Rs 3.14 lakh crore estimated tax saved by large firms over ~5 years; BSE 500 effective tax rate fell from >30% (to FY19) to 21.2% (FY24); evidence of higher private investment called mixed/inconclusive (pandemic confounder).
outcome_metric: estimated revenue foregone; effective tax rate
side_effects: Revenue loss; profits went partly into reserves and current assets
public_reaction: Economists quoted sceptical (Nagaraj: no Laffer effect evidence)
source_title: Lower Tax Rates Saved Big Firms Rs 3.14 Lakh Crore Since 2019: Report (The Wire, 28 Nov 2024)

description: Incentives tied to incremental sales over a base year across 14 sectors; total outlay Rs 1.97 lakh crore; launched April 2020.
stated_goal: Scale up domestic manufacturing, exports and jobs; reduce imports
outcome_summary: Govt data: actual investment Rs 2.16 lakh crore and 14.39 lakh jobs (to 31 Dec 2025); cumulative sales Rs 20.41 lakh crore; exports Rs 8.3 lakh crore; incentives disbursed Rs 28,748 crore; mobile phone imports down ~77% since FY21; electronics production up 146% FY21-FY25.
side_effects: Disbursal small relative to outlay; no counterfactual; sector-level underperformance not reported in official docs
public_reaction: Not verified from an opened source in this pass
source_title: PLI scheme investments cross Rs 2.16 lakh crore, over 14.39 lakh jobs created (IANS, citing Ministry of Commerce, 20 Feb 2026)

policy_name: PAHAL - Direct Benefit Transfer for LPG (DBTL)
description: LPG sold at market price with subsidy credited to Aadhaar/bank-linked accounts; launched Nov 2014 in 54 districts, nationwide from Jan 2015; paired with Give It Up campaign.
stated_goal: Cut leakages/diversion and duplicate connections; reduce subsidy bill
outcome_summary: CAG: LPG subsidy payout fell Rs 23,316 crore in 2015-16 but 92% was due to the crude price fall; govt claimed PAHAL savings Rs 9,211 crore, OMCs Rs 5,107 crore, CAG recalculated Rs 4,813 crore (Rs 3,473 crore after Give It Up adjustment); 6.72 million gave up subsidy.
outcome_metric: LPG subsidy savings attributable to PAHAL (2015-16)
outcome_value: CAG Rs 3,473-4,813 crore vs govt claim Rs 9,211 crore
side_effects: Savings overstated by govt; ineligible/blocked consumers assumed to draw full quota
public_reaction: Not verified from an opened source in this pass
source_title: Savings in LPG subsidy: Now, CAG says 92% claimed saving due to crude price drop (Moneylife, 16 Aug 2016, on CAG Report 25 of 2016)

description: 122 2G licences with spectrum issued in 2008 at prices discovered in 2001, without auction.
stated_goal: Expand telecom competition and coverage
outcome_summary: CAG estimated presumptive loss of Rs 1,76,379 crore; Supreme Court (Feb 2012) cancelled all 122 licences as unconstitutional and arbitrary and ordered re-auction; base price for 5 MHz set at Rs 14,000 crore; CBI special court acquitted all 18 accused on 21 Dec 2017.
side_effects: Licence cancellation, regulatory uncertainty; loss figure disputed by govt at the time
public_reaction: Major political scandal; 2017 acquittal reopened debate on CAG estimate
source_title: 2G scam verdict: A Raja, Kanimozhi, CAG Vinod Rai spectrum (Business Today)

policy_name: Coal block allocation by screening committee (1993-2011) and SC cancellation
description: 218 coal blocks allocated administratively 1993-2011; SC held them arbitrary and illegal (Aug 2014) and cancelled 204 (Sep 2014).
stated_goal: Secure captive coal supply for core industries
outcome_summary: CAG Performance Audit 7 of 2012-13 estimated Rs 1.86 lakh crore financial gains to private parties; SC cancelled 204 blocks; 42 producing blocks paid additional levy of Rs 295/tonne until 31 Mar 2015; Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act 2015 mandated e-auction.
outcome_metric: CAG estimated gain to private allottees
side_effects: Disruption and re-allocation of 204 blocks
public_reaction: Major political scandal ('Coalgate')
source_title: CAG Compliance Audit on e-Auction of Coal Mines, Chapter 1 (2016)

description: E-auction of cancelled coal blocks under the Coal Mines (Special Provisions) Act 2015; 29 mines auctioned in two tranches Feb-Mar 2015 per CAG.
stated_goal: Transparent price discovery; revenue for coal-bearing states
outcome_summary: Business Today (9 Mar 2015): cumulative bids of ~Rs 1.57 lakh crore for roughly 30 blocks, close to the CAG loss estimate; first 19 mines raised Rs 1.10 lakh crore per PM. A 2018 The Wire report (title only seen) says realised receipts were far below govt estimates.
side_effects: Realised revenue later reported far below estimates (not verified in detail)
public_reaction: Govt cited it as proof the scam was real
source_title: Coal auction rains revenue bonanza, touches Rs 1.57 lakh cr (Business Today)

description: RBI Act amended May 2016; Monetary Policy Committee targets 4% CPI inflation with 2-6% band; failure = 3 consecutive quarters outside band; target retained in 2021.
stated_goal: Price stability with growth; anchor inflation expectations
outcome_summary: Average CPI inflation fell from 6.8% (2012-16) to 4.9% since adoption; std. deviation 2.3% to 1.5%; inflation within 2-6% band ~3/4 of time in first review period and ~2/3 in second; breached during COVID and Russia-Ukraine shocks.
outcome_metric: average CPI inflation pre vs post FIT
side_effects: Band breaches during supply shocks
public_reaction: Not verified from an opened source in this pass
source_title: Review of Monetary Policy Framework by RBI (PRS India summary of RBI discussion paper, 2025)

description: Diesel prices made market-determined from 18 Oct 2014 (petrol earlier in 2010), ending under-recovery compensation for diesel.
stated_goal: Reduce fiscal subsidy and OMC under-recoveries
outcome_summary: Diesel under-recoveries Apr-Dec 2014 fell 77% to Rs 10,935 crore from Rs 47,655 crore; total fuel under-recoveries down 33%; petroleum subsidy projected to fall to Rs 38,000 crore in FY15 from Rs 85,000 crore in FY14 - but crude basket also fell 52%, confounding attribution.
side_effects: Timing coincided with crude crash, so savings partly windfall
public_reaction: Not verified from an opened source in this pass
source_title: OMCs' under-recoveries shrink by a third in April-Dec period (Business Standard, 23 Jan 2015)

target_group: NREGS workers and social security pension (SSP) beneficiaries
description: Biometric Smartcards and bank-led last-mile payment for NREGS wages and pensions, randomized across 296 sub-districts in 8 districts (~19 million people)
stated_goal: Reduce payment delays and leakage in welfare payments
outcome_summary: Payments arrived 6-10 days sooner; collection time fell 22 minutes (20%); NREGS beneficiary earnings rose 24% with unchanged government outlays, implying leakage fell 41% (NREGS) and 47% (SSP); 90-93% of beneficiaries preferred Smartcards
side_effects: Incomplete rollout: only ~half of payments in treatment areas went through the new system after two years
public_reaction: 90% of NREGS and 93% of SSP beneficiaries preferred Smartcards (survey)
source_title: J-PAL policy brief: Smartcards for Smarter Payments

description: Aadhaar-based biometric authentication (ABBA) at ration shops randomized across 132 blocks in 10 districts; followed by a reconciliation policy holding undistributed stock against dealers
stated_goal: Reduce leakage/corruption in PDS grain distribution
outcome_summary: ABBA did not significantly reduce leakage (control leakage ~20% of value); beneficiary transaction costs rose 17% (Rs 7 on Rs 41); probability of receiving nothing rose 2.4 pp (~296,000 people); unseeded households lost Rs 49 (12.6%); 1.5-2 million people lost benefits at some point
side_effects: Exclusion errors: 1.2-1.7 million newly excluded during reconciliation; unsuccessful trips doubled
public_reaction: Activists linked hunger deaths to Aadhaar failures (see news row)
source_title: Identity Verification Standards in Welfare Programs: Experimental Evidence from India (NBER WP 26744)

description: Mandatory Aadhaar linkage/authentication for rations
stated_goal: Reduce leakage in PDS
outcome_summary: Activists compiled 42 hunger-related deaths since 2017 of which 25 were linked to Aadhaar issues; list marked one year since death of 11-year-old Santoshi Kumari in Jharkhand
outcome_metric: Hunger deaths linked to Aadhaar issues (activist count)
side_effects: Exclusion of legitimate beneficiaries
public_reaction: Strong civil-society backlash; activist lists of starvation deaths
source_title: Of 42 Hunger-Related Deaths Since 2017, 25 Linked to Aadhaar Issues (The Wire, 21 Sep 2018)

policy_name: Bihar Mukhyamantri Cycle Yojana (bicycles for girls)
description: Bicycles given to girls who enrolled in secondary school
stated_goal: Close gender gap in secondary enrollment
outcome_summary: Girls' age-appropriate secondary enrollment rose 30%; gender gap fell 40%; larger gains where secondary school was farther away; more cost-effective than comparable South Asian CCTs
side_effects: None reported in abstract
public_reaction: Not assessed
source_title: Cycling to School: Increasing Secondary School Enrollment for Girls in India (NBER WP 19305)

target_group: Pregnant women (poor, rural) and supporting health workers
description: Conditional cash incentive for delivering in government or accredited facilities, plus incentive to the health worker
stated_goal: Reduce maternal and neonatal mortality by raising institutional deliveries
outcome_summary: Higher antenatal care and facility births; 4 fewer perinatal deaths per 1,000 pregnancies and 2 fewer neonatal deaths per 1,000 live births; maternal mortality effect undetermined
side_effects: Uptake varied 5%-44% across states (2007-08); poorest and least educated participated slightly less
public_reaction: Not assessed
source_title: IHME summary of Lim et al. (2010) Lancet evaluation of JSY

description: Government-funded hospitalisation insurance (cover Rs 30,000)
stated_goal: Financial protection for hospital care
outcome_summary: Utilisation rose (LTI hospitalisation +1.3 pp/16%; doctor treatment for STI +3.2 pp/7.6%; lost days -20.8%) but monthly per-capita OOP spending rose Rs 46.3 (37%), concentrated at upper quantiles
side_effects: OOP spending increased rather than fell
public_reaction: Not assessed
source_title: How RSBY impacted healthcare utilisation and spending (Ideas for India; Dutta and Sarkar 2021, IHDS)

target_group: ~50 crore poor and vulnerable people (potential beneficiaries)
description: Rs 5 lakh per family per year cover for secondary/tertiary hospitalisation, 16x RSBY cover
stated_goal: Financial protection; reduce catastrophic health spending
outcome_summary: 17.86 crore cards issued by Mar 2022 (just over a third of eligible); studies mixed - Garg et al. (2020) find no rise in hospitalisation in Chhattisgarh and Bala et al./Garg et al. find no fall in catastrophic spending; some facility studies report benefits
side_effects: Excludes outpatient care (~55% of OOPE) and medicines (53% of OOPE); admissions fell from 22 to 13 lakh/quarter in Apr-Jun 2020
public_reaction: Not assessed
source_title: Assessing Ayushman Bharat: Has it Enhanced the Financial Protection of Indians? (SPRF)

description: Subsidised household latrine construction and behaviour-change campaign to end open defecation
stated_goal: Eliminate open defecation
outcome_summary: Improved sanitation rose ~18 pp all-India and ~23 pp in rural Bihar (to 45.7%) between NFHS-4 and NFHS-5; open defecation in BR/MP/RJ/UP estimated to fall from 70.2% to ~50%
side_effects: Large residual open defecation (~200 million rural people in focus states) despite ODF claims; household-level surveys understate individual open defecation
public_reaction: Not assessed
source_title: What can we learn about Swachh Bharat Mission from the NFHS-5 factsheets? (Coffey, Franz, Spears; Ideas for India)

description: No-frills bank accounts with RuPay debit cards
stated_goal: Universal access to bank accounts
outcome_summary: 545.5 million PMJDY accounts in PSBs by Sep 2025; 56% held by women; average balance Rs 4,768 (up 3.7x in a decade); but 26% of PSB accounts inoperative (up from 21% a year earlier)
outcome_metric: Share of PSB PMJDY accounts inoperative
side_effects: Dormancy; 31% of accounts without RuPay cards; Findex: 35% of Indian account holders inactive by 2021
public_reaction: Not assessed
game_theory_lens: signalling / target-driven account opening (principal-agent: banks vs government)
source_title: 26% of Jan Dhan accounts with PSBs inactive as usage slows (Business Standard, 15 Oct 2025)

description: Free cooked meals in government schools
stated_goal: Improve nutrition, attendance and learning
outcome_summary: Young Lives AP data: for drought-affected young children, meal effect +0.484 SD weight-for-age and +1.581 SD height-for-age (offsetting drought losses); older cohort vocabulary scores +0.775-0.794 SD vs private-school peers (PSM)
side_effects: No effect on nutrition for older children (11-12); brief has labelling inconsistencies and no significance stars on meal effects
public_reaction: Not assessed
source_title: Young Lives Policy Brief 8: The Impact of the Midday Meal Scheme on Nutrition and Learning

description: Unaided non-minority private schools reserve at least 25% of entry-level seats; state reimburses fees
stated_goal: Socially integrated schooling for disadvantaged children
outcome_summary: 2013-14: ~610,000 of ~21.1 million seats filled (29% fill rate, up from 21.5%); only ~45,000 of 206,000 private schools admitted any child; UP <1%, AP <5%; Rajasthan and MP half of all admissions
side_effects: Delayed/inadequate reimbursement; opaque state rules; school reluctance
public_reaction: Private schools reluctant; complaints on reimbursement
source_title: Reservation under RTE: Status of implementation and way forward (Ideas for India; State of the Nation RTE 12(1)(c) 2015)

target_group: Male drinkers; women facing intimate partner violence
description: Complete state-wide ban on sale, purchase, consumption and manufacture of alcohol (April 2016)
stated_goal: Reduce alcohol abuse and associated domestic violence
outcome_summary: In higher pre-ban alcohol blocks, women 4.2-12% less likely to face physical violence and 7.4% less likely to face emotional violence; 6.3 pp fewer spousal restrictions; effect larger with more SHGs
side_effects: Smuggling/bootlegging, spurious-alcohol deaths, lost excise revenue, diverted policing, possible substitution to other substances
public_reaction: See news row: mass arrests and High Court criticism
source_title: Impact of Bihar's alcohol ban on intimate partner violence (Ideas for India; Debnath, Paul, Sareen 2023)

description: Enforcement under the Bihar Prohibition and Excise Act 2016
stated_goal: Reduce alcohol consumption
outcome_summary: 8.69 lakh people arrested under the liquor law up to 14 May 2023; Patna High Court criticised police collusion with smugglers and burden on daily wagers (Nov 2024 report)
side_effects: Over-criminalisation of poor; police-smuggler collusion
public_reaction: Judicial criticism; political opposition
source_title: HC Slams Bihar's Liquor Prohibition Act (The Wire, 16 Nov 2024)

policy_name: Delhi pink ticket (free bus travel for women)
target_group: All women bus riders in Delhi (universal)
description: Zero-fare travel for women on DTC and DIMTS buses from Oct 2019
stated_goal: Improve women's mobility and access
outcome_summary: Women's share of bus ridership 25% (2020-21) to 33% (2022-23); survey (n=510): 23% travel more by bus, 15% of rare users now regular, 54% report saving money
side_effects: Safety gaps remain (poor lighting, harassment, long waits); evidence largely perception-based
public_reaction: Critics call it voter bait/fiscally irresponsible; scheme copied by Tamil Nadu, Punjab, Karnataka
source_title: A Free Ticket Can Be a Ticket to Freedom (The India Forum)

target_group: Girl children; districts with low child sex ratio
description: Awareness/advocacy campaign with funds to states
stated_goal: Improve child sex ratio and girls' education
outcome_summary: Parliamentary Committee on Empowerment of Women: 78.91% of Rs 446.72 crore released 2016-2019 spent on media advocacy; states spent only 25.13% of Rs 622.48 crore given; outcome on sex ratio not measured in source
outcome_metric: Share of released funds spent on media advocacy
side_effects: Funds concentrated on advertising; low state utilisation
public_reaction: Opposition criticism after the parliamentary panel report
source_title: Nearly 80% of Beti Bachao funds spent on media, House panel expresses dismay (Newslaundry, 10 Dec 2021)
